title: CLCON/150/2017 of Prem Singh Vs Mrs Aradhana Shukla

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Civil Contempt Petition No.150 of 2017
Prem Singh .......... Contempt-Petitioner
versus
Mrs. Aradhana Shukla and others ......Respondents
Mr. Yogesh Kumar Pacholia, learned counsel for the contempt
petitioner.
Mr. I.D.Paliwal, learned counsel for the respondent no.1/State of Uttar
Pradesh.
Mr. Arvind Vashisth, learned Senior Counsel, assisted by Ms. Monika
Pant, learned Counsel for the respondent nos. 2 & 4/Uttar Pradesh
Road Transport Corporation.
Mr. Ashish Joshi, learned counsel for the respondent no.3.
-----------
Judgement dated: 20.07.2022
Hon'ble Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.
Upon hearing the learned counsels, the Court made the
following Order.
1. By filing the contempt petition, the petitioner
seeks the following reliefs:
"It is therefore most respectfully prayed that this
Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to summon
the opposite party/respondents and penalize them
with exemplary punishment for floating and
committing the gorses contempt of the order passed
by this Hon'ble Court on 10.01.2017 in Special
Appeal No. 105 of 2014, U.P. State Road Transport
Corporation vs. Prem Singh, and furthermore this
Hon'ble Court may direct the contemnor to comply
the aforesaid order passed by this Hon'ble Court,
otherwise petitioner will suffer irreparable loss and
injury."

2
2. It is brought to our notice that in a Bunch of
Special Appeals decided by the Hon'ble Division
Bench including the Special Appeal of the
present petitioner i.e. Special Appeal No. 105 of
2014, vide judgement dated 10.01.2017,
wherein the following observations were made
in para 43.
"Therefore, having regard to the above
discussion, we dispose of the Appeals as follows:
In Special Appeal Appeals Nos. 56 of 2014, 57 of
2014, 58 of 2014, 59 of 2014, 60 of 2014, 105 of
2014, 431 of 2015, 433 of 2015, 437 of 2015, 440 of
2015, 442 of 2015, 460 of 2015, 462 of 2015, 548 of
2015, as being cases of the persons, who claim to
be appointed prior to 1960, we direct that the
Corporation will look into their records and ascertain
whether they are permanent employees in terms of
the 1960 orders and if they are permanent
employees in terms of the Government Orders and
as explained by us, they will be granted pensionary
benefits on condition, of course, that they will return
benefits of Provident Fund, which they already
claimed and which was disbursed to them. They will
not be entitled to interest as they are also agreeable
for amount being returned without interest. They will
also not be liable to pay interest and they will also
not claim interest. This exercise should be
completed by the Corporation within a period of four
months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of
this judgment. In Special Appeal No. 57 of 2014, the
issue relates to the period a little more than a year.
Since he is already being paid pension and only the
question is whether he is entitled to count certain 39
period, namely, period between 08.02.1951 to

3
21.07.1952, we direct that the respondent will
consider the same and take a decision within a
period of two months and communicate the same to
the employee.
The other Appeals, which arise from the
judgment of Hon'ble Justice Sudhanshu Dhulia, will
stand dismissed. The other Appeals by Mr. Arvind
Vashisth and Mr. Ashish Joshi will stand allowed
and the writ petitions will stand dismissed. Appeal
No. 57 of 2014 will stand disposed of."
3. Therefore, as there were Bunch of Appeals, a
number of petitioners' cases were considered on
the facts and were decided, the Hon'ble Court
instead of giving a specific direction to the
respondents/contemnors, passed the Order
mentioned above.
4. Learned senior counsel Mr. Arvind Vashishth
would submit that in their counter affidavit
they have taken specific plea that the
corporation has examined the case of the
petitioner and has come to the conclusion that
as he is not a permanent employee in terms of
1960 orders and, therefore, it is not possible to
give him pension.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner, on the other
hand, would submit that the decision taken by
the respondents is contrary to the observations
made by the Hon'ble Division Bench and,
therefore, the Contempt will lie against them.

4
6. This court is of the opinion that as there is no
specific direction to the respondent to grant
pensionery benefits to the petitioner, he cannot
be given the benefit of pension by this Court,
while deciding the contempt petition. Whether
the decision taken by the Corporation is not in
the light of the decision pronounced by the
Hon'ble Division Bench in para 43 of the
judgement mentioned above should be decided
as a fresh cause of action. However, the
petitioner may initiate afresh writ application
before this Court for decision and specific
direction to grant him pensionry benefits.
7. At this stage, this Court is of the opinion that
the respondent-contemnor has not committed
any deliberate and willful disobedience of the
Court's Order rather they might have decided
the case of the petitioner in erroneously and for
that, contempt proceeding cannot be initiated
against the respondents/contemnors. However,
we give liberty the petitioner to approach this
Court by filing a proper writ application raising
his grievance regarding the pensionery benefits.
 (S.K.Mishra, J.)
 (Urgent copy of the order as per rules)
